To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MPI is an effective programming paradigm for the parallel implementation of the ELFM, that the use of checkpointing and roll-back can significantly enhance the performance of the MPI implementation, and that the parallel performance of MPI implementation of ELFM is sensitive to the number of processors.
the parallel implementation of the ELFM using MPI and checkpointing is efficient and can be applied to other models with similar parallel application model.
the performance of a parallel implementation of the ELFM using MPI is significantly improved using the proposed synchronous checkpointing mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the parallel implementation of the ELFM using checkpointing.
the parallel implementation of a large scale, dynamic and irregular simulation model.
the development of an efficient parallel implementation of an irregularly structured and dynamic model, the ELFM, on a NOW using MPI and checkpointing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the checkpointing and rollback mechanism is a promising approach to the parallelization of ELFM and other applications with similar parallelization features.
the MPI-based parallel implementation of ELFM with checkpointing and rollback is an efficient parallel implementation of ELFMs.
checkpointing and rollback are effective and efficient for parallelizing the Everglades landscape fire model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed parallel ELFM code is efficient in terms of performance and scalability.
checkpointing and rollback are very useful for irregular and asynchronous computation, especially when the computation is dynamic and the data are large.
the parallel ELFM is efficient and effective for the simulation of fire propagation and spread in a large scale landscape, such as the Everglades National Park in South Florida, USA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of checkpointing and the developed parallel application model can significantly improve the performance of the parallel implementation of ELFM.

the checkpointing and rollback technologies can be effectively applied in a parallel application model with a mixture of a variety synchronous and asynchronous computations, where the synchronous computation is intermittent, and the length of each synchronous operation is variable.
the checkpointing mechanism is a very effective tool in the parallel implementation of the ELFM.
